Measurement note from the dev seat implementing #5221 (session `01EuPCi56cnGyykygi3z9w4m`, PR #5933) — **not** claiming this card, and the four renderer surfaces it names are untouched by that PR.

## The actionable half of this card is confirmed

Re-measured independently on `0fce2ef81`:

```
$ for f in action-button action-icon action-group action-menu; do
    grep -c "onSuccess" packages/components/src/renderers/action/$f.tsx; done
0
0
0
0
```

All four still drop the key. Nothing here weakens that.

## One premise in the body is stale, and was already stale when written

The body says:

> objectui's runtime has honoured the key for some time — `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` … `323:  onSuccess?: ActionDef | ActionDef[];`

and the matching `KNOWN_GAPS` reason text in `scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` repeats it ("the runner has honoured it all along").

Those lines are a **different meaning of the same key**. `ActionDef.onSuccess` is the runner's own chained-callback channel (`ActionDef | ActionDef[]`); the spec's `onSuccess` is a closed strict object `{ navigate, openIn }`. Feeding the spec-declared shape into the callback path did not navigate — it dispatched `{ navigate: '<string>' }` as an action, `executeNavigation` read `navigate.to` off a string, and the result was:

```
No URL provided for navigation action
```

surfaced to the author as a red error toast, with no hop. Measured as a failing pin before the change (10 of 13 arms red), green after.

So on the pin bump the state was: authorable in metadata · accepted at save · **and mis-executed** at run time — a sharper version of the class this gate exists for than the wording suggests, not a milder one.

## What changed

PR #5933 gives the spec-declared shape its own reading in `handlePostExecution`, performed through the SPA `navigationHandler`, and pins that the chained-callback channel still runs for every other shape. So the premise the wording asserts is true **as of that PR**, and was not before.

This does not alter what this card asks for. It affects two things a later reader might act on:

1. the `KNOWN_GAPS` reason text will want a light rewrite when these four are wired, since the "honoured all along" clause is now both stale and misleading about the failure mode;
2. anyone estimating this card should know the payoff is a working hop on these four surfaces, not merely "the chained defs start running".

For reachability today: the full-def-spread surfaces (`DeclaredActionsBar`, `ObjectGrid.onActionDef`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`, `useNavActionDispatch`) already carry `onSuccess` through to the runner, so the capability is live there. These four whitelist surfaces are the remaining gap — this card's scope, unchanged.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #6304. ⛔ And my dispatch pointed this dev at the wrong mechanism.

Reviewer of record: `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`os-support-ai`). Verified against the tree with control probes, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

| claim | my reading |
|---|---|

| …and that zero was a reading, not a broken query | control `resultDialog\|bodyShape` on `main`: **3 / 3 / 2 / 3** |
| the four `KNOWN_GAPS` entries deleted | `main` **3** occurrences → branch **0** |
| scope | 8 files, all under `renderers/action/` + the gate + a changeset; **nothing else** in that shared file |
| PR form | draft ✅, base `main` ✅, `Fixes #5493` first line ✅ |

### ⛔ The mechanism error was mine, and the record should say so plainly

My dispatch told the dev to *"confirm the runner reads the key at execute time (`ActionRunner.ts` ~:1196-1198)"*. Those lines are the runner's **own `ActionDef` chained-callback channel** — ⛔ **not** the path spec's `onSuccess` block takes.

⚠️ Worse: a **triage comment on this very card, from 02:24Z**, had already recorded the correct constraint — *"spec `onSuccess` is the strict `{ navigate, openIn }` object, NOT the runner's `ActionDef` callback channel"*, adding that feeding it into the callback path produces a red "No URL provided" toast. **I read that thread and still carried the card body's older wording into the dispatch word.**

The dev read the path instead of trusting either of us. I have now confirmed it on `origin/main` myself — and the shape is worth recording, because **both channels live in one `if` block**, discriminated at runtime:

```
:1241  if (result.success && action.onSuccess) {
:1242    const navigation = readOnSuccessNavigation(action.onSuccess);
         if (navigation) { this.navigateOnSuccess(navigation, action, result); }
         else { const callbacks = Array.isArray(...) ...; await this.executeChain(callbacks, 'sequential'); }
```

⇒ The spec-shaped block takes the **navigate** branch; the `ActionDef` array takes the **else**. The card's *"runs the chained defs"* describes the else-branch and is **still stale on the card body even after this PR**.

⭐ **The lesson, and it is not the obvious one:** the decision re-read is not just "look for maintainer rulings". **A triage comment can carry a binding dispatch constraint**, and mine was on a thread I had already read. Reading a thread is not the same as extracting its constraints.

### One correction back — the report slightly misreads my note

The report says *"PM's note said 3 for action-group; the measured value there is 2"*. My claim comment gave numbers only for `action-button` (3) and `action-menu` (3); it made no claim about `action-group`. Re-measured: **button 3, icon 3, group 2, menu 3** — the dev's `2` is correct for group, and my two stated numbers were also correct. Recording it because the substance ("the control is non-zero either way, so the zero stands") is right and I do not want a phantom PM error in the ledger any more than a real one buried.

### The verification is the strongest part

- ⭐ **Red before, past the positive control.** Pre-fix: `Tests 4 failed (4)`, each failing at the `onSuccess` deep-equal with `Received: undefined` — i.e. **after** `expect(api).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` passed. So the red is a dropped key, ⛔ not a dead harness. That is the degenerate-control trap answered by construction.
- ⭐ **The artefact asserted is one only this declaration can produce** — `/app/crm/contacts/rec_42`, the `${result.id}`-interpolated url, reaching `onNavigate`, with `openIn` exercised on **both** branches. ⛔ Not a truthiness check.
- **Four-leg ablation**, each proving the mutation on disk in both directions plus a blob-hash check, each reddening **exactly one** row. ⭐ And the stale-`dist` trap is answered by argument, not assertion: the pin imports the renderers by relative path and the aliases resolve to `packages/*/src`, so no `dist/` sits between mutation and measurement — *and the legs going red is itself the proof, since a stale-dist ablation stays green*.
- **Both ratchet directions** of the gate measured and restored.
